segments.text: Lesson 22
segments.translation: 第22课

segments.text: By heart
segments.translation: 熟记

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: Which actor read the letter in the end, the aristocrat or the gaoler?
segments.translation: 最后是哪位演员读的信，是那位贵族还是那位狱卒？

segments.text: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
segments.translation: 有些剧目非常成功，以致连续演出好几年。

segments.text: In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
segments.translation: 在很多方面，这对可怜的演员们来说是不幸的，因为他们被要求夜复一夜地重复同样的台词。

segments.text: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
segments.translation: 人们本以为他们能熟记自己的台词，绝不会有结巴的时候。

segments.text: Yet this is not always the case.
segments.translation: 然而，情况并不总是这样。

segments.text: A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for twenty years.
segments.translation: 一位著名演员在一部非常成功的戏剧中扮演一位被囚禁在巴士底狱20年的贵族。

segments.text: In the last act, a gaoler would always come on to the stage with a letter which he would hand to the prisoner.
segments.translation: 在最后一幕中，一个狱卒总是拿着一封信走上舞台，把信交给囚犯。

segments.text: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
segments.translation: 虽然那位贵族理应在每次演出时读这封信，但他总是坚持信要完整地写出来。

segments.text: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if, after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
segments.translation: 一天晚上，狱卒决定对他的同事开个玩笑，看看经过这么多场演出，他是否已经能背出信的内容了。

segments.text: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
segments.translation: 幕拉开了，是戏的最后一幕，露出了那位贵族独自坐在阴暗牢房的铁窗后面。

segments.text: Just then, the gaoler appeared with the precious letter in his hands.
segments.translation: 就在这时，狱卒手里拿着那封珍贵的信出现了。

segments.text: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.
segments.translation: 他走进牢房，把信交给那位贵族。

segments.text: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.
segments.translation: 但他给他的那张信纸并没有像往常那样写满字。

segments.text: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
segments.translation: 那只是一张白纸。

segments.text: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
segments.translation: 狱卒急切地看着，渴望看到他的演员同事是否终于学会了他的台词。

segments.text: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.
segments.translation: 那位贵族盯着那张白纸看了几秒钟。

segments.text: Then, squinting his eyes, he said: 'The light is dim. Read the letter to me.'
segments.translation: 然后，他眯起眼睛说：“光线太暗。请读信给我听。”

segments.text: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the gaoler.
segments.translation: 他随即把那张纸递给了狱卒。

segments.text: Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either, the gaoler replied: 'The light is indeed dim, sire.  I must get my glasses.  '
segments.translation: 狱卒发现自己也记不得信上的一个字，于是回答说：“陛下，光线确实太暗了。我得去拿眼镜。”

segments.text: With this, he hurried off the stage.
segments.translation: 说完，他急忙跑下了舞台。

segments.text: Much to the aristocrat's amusement, the gaoler returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.
segments.translation: 使那位贵族感到非常好笑的是，狱卒过了一会儿带着一副眼镜和往常那封写满字的信回来了，并开始读给囚犯听。
